chunks: And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from al-Fudayl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Muslim who lends a loan to another Muslim seeking thereby the countenance of Allah, except that its reward is recorded for him with the accounting of charity, until it returns to him.'

key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The countenance/face of Allah (seeking divine pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for lending money to a fellow Muslim in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the spiritual merit of *Qard al-Hasan* (benevolent loan) as a sustained act of worship. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the reward is not merely for the initial act of lending but continues incrementally until the principal is returned, emphasizing the lender's sincerity (*Ikhlas*) in seeking Allah's pleasure rather than material gain.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “One who grants a loan to a believer it is considered as Sadaqah by Allah and he will get the reward of giving Sadaqah.”
